details:
AURA (Autonomous Space Health & Triage) is an offline-first daily health companion, interactive 3D anatomical copilot, and zero-latency emergency response web application (aura-space-health.replit.app) built by Team Momentum (Daiwik Patel and Nimish Patel) for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Designed specifically for deep-space missions like Mars transit legs, AURA empowers crews to maintain health and handle crises independently during severe 44-minute communication blackouts.

Core Modules & Functionality

AURA unifies mission health management into four intuitive, on-device modules backed by NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) baselines:

  1. Body Module: Features an interactive 3D anatomical twin with drag-to-rotate, scroll-to-zoom, and posterior/anterior toggle controls (Show back/Spin). Tapping any zone (e.g., chest or shoulder) opens a dedicated AI chat copilot grounded in spaceflight health biology with isolated per-region conversation memory.
  2. Analytics Module: Overlays spacecraft life-support telemetry directly onto crew vitals—tracking resting heart rate against ambient carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) accumulation across a 14-sol history with a 7-sol predictive drift forecast based on NASA Biological & Physical Sciences (BPS) response curves. Mission milestone markers tie biometric spikes to events like EVA prep and scrubber swaps.
  3. Checkpoints Module: Drives daily crew compliance through a 2-minute Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) for cognitive alertness and an interactive Left/Right eye Amsler grid to catch Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) early. Crew members can tag structured ocular symptoms (Wavy lines, Missing areas, Blurry patches, Dark spots) which instantly generate color-coded Nominal (green) or Watch (amber) triage logs stored locally in the browser.
  4. Red Shift (Emergency Mode): Instantly transforms the interface into a stark, hazard-striped black console during cabin emergencies. It features safety confirmation gates ("Is the area safe for responders?"), an interactive 3D bay and drawer mini-map guiding crew to assets like Bay 4, Drawer B (Defibrillator) and Med Rack 2, Upper (ECG), and animated 5-step hardware operation walkthroughs for ECGs, AEDs, pulse oximeters, blood-pressure monitors, and ultrasound devices.

Intended Impact & Technology

AURA eliminates reliance on real-time ground control, mitigating physiological drift, cognitive fatigue, and medical emergencies autonomously. Built using custom HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript with 100% on-device browser persistence, Team Momentum’s dual-mode architecture successfully bridges the gap between calm, routine wellness tracking and high-stress emergency execution.
